title: Audit Log
markdown:
The audit log is a persistent, searchable, append-only record of what the system did — distinct from episodic memory (which biases future LLM behavior). Every event flows through `audit/logger.log_event`, a synchronous SQLite writer (WAL + 5s busy_timeout) that appends one row to the `audit_log` table in `episodic_memory.db`.

### Event types
Rows are tagged by `event_type`, including `chat_turn`, `specialist_consult`, `tool_invocation`, `scheduled_action`, `alert`, `integration_inbound` (Slack / Discord / email / Telegram / Google Chat), plus `knowledge_retrieval`, `memory_extraction` (one row per episodic-extraction pass, written in a `finally` so a crashed pass is recorded too: how many items the model proposed, how many were stored, a `{kind, reason}` record per drop, a `malformed` count for payload shapes that were never usable items, and a `failure` naming the exception type when the pass raised — including `CancelledError`, which is a `BaseException` and so would otherwise be logged as a clean empty pass — a `proposed>0, stored=0` streak means the quote validator is rejecting everything, which is otherwise invisible), `cache_event` (one row per model call from every call site — Executive turns, specialist consults (chat turns and workflow steps), research specialists, the research routing and watchlist passes, triage, memory extraction — carrying tokens, cache hits, cost, server-side search count and, inside a research run, its `run_id`), `memory_snapshot`, `committee_review`, `peer_memory`, `attunement` (one row per open-loop extraction pass — opened / closed / dropped with a reason per drop and a `failure` type — plus a row per loop opened or closed and per 👍/👎 on a reply; see Attunement), `executive_paused` / `executive_resumed` (the operator pause switch; actor is the caller's email, details carry the reason, or on resume the held-action count), `scheduled_action_cancelled` (a pending scheduled action cancelled from the Pulse page or a script; actor is the signed-in email, `admin-token` or `local`), `workspace_settings_changed` (solo/team mode, the user's time zone or the principal's role changed through `PUT /workspace`; actor is the caller's email or `api`, details carry the mode's and zone's from/to, plus `role_fields_changed` — the names of the role fields that changed, never their text — when the role changed), `decision_class_mode_changed` (a decision class switched between `propose` and `auto_execute` through `PUT /decisions/classes/meeting_scheduling`; same actor rule, details carry the class and the mode's from/to), the four Act as me events — `delegation_settings_changed` (a person turned it on or off for themselves), `delegation_gmail_verified` (their own Gmail checked before turning it on), `delegation_voice_changed` ("How I write" learned, edited, locked or reset, or its signature read from Gmail again) and `delegation_drafted` (one per draft saved in their Gmail) — always private and metadata only: ids, counts and flags, never the draft or the thread; and the external-signal/monitor events.

### Session & turn context
Each row carries `session_id`, `turn_id`, `actor`, `summary`, `details_json`, `full_json`, `department`, and `private_to_principal`. A `turn_id` (`f"t-{uuid12}"`) is set per Executive turn and propagated automatically via ContextVars to retriever / specialist / tool / cache emits, grouping one user-assistant exchange. `summary` is the searchable column (LIKE, ~300 char cap); `details_json` is structured and not searched. `department` is filterable in SQL (`AuditLogger.query(department=…)`) — the department check-in's skip rule uses it to ask whether anything was logged for a department since its Goals were last reviewed.

### Rows private to the principal
Every signed-in user can read `/audit`, so a row about something private to the principal is marked `private_to_principal` as it is written, and only the principal reads it. `AuditLogger.log` marks a row private when its caller passes `private=True` — the email poller's two inbound rows for mail from one of the principal's contacts or mail they forwarded, and `create_alert`'s row for a private alert — or when `people_tools.audit_row_private_to_principal` says so at write time:
- every row a turn private to the principal writes (`Session.private_to_principal`): its reply, each tool call, the model-call rows, and the background passes that inherit the turn;
- on the principal's own verified turn (or inside `grant_contact_egress`), any row whose summary, details or full payload names one of their contacts — their email address or full name anywhere in the text, or their person id or chat id in a person or recipient field (`person_id`, `attendee_person_ids`, `user_id`, `chat_id`, `channel_ref`), JSON tool results included.
- every row an Act as me turn writes once `ghostwrite_email` has touched the speaker's mailbox (`TurnDelegation.touched_mail`, set before the tool's first read): the tool row, the reply's `chat_turn` row carrying the draft's preview, the model-call rows, and anything it starts in the background, under `private_rows` (it runs no learning passes). Only the principal can have Act as me for now, so private to the principal is the right visibility; the tool's input and result are also redacted (`ghostwrite` is a sensitive tool name).

Some rows are written before their turn binds its session, so two scopes in `audit.context` count too. The email poller holds `private_rows` for the whole handling of a mail from a contact or a principal forward: every row is private, the knowledge retrieval (which quotes the mail) included. The chat adapters hold `principal_turn_rows` once they know the principal sent the message on a verified surface (`people_tools.audit_rows_on_senders_turn` on Slack, Discord and Telegram; the web chat route checks its caller), so the inbound row, the knowledge retrieval, alert triage and the start of the web stream follow the principal-turn rule above. Tasks started inside inherit the scope, except unattended work: a workflow run a chat reply resumes and each scheduled action start with neither (`unscoped_audit_rows`), so their rows follow the ordinary rule. A sender lookup that fails counts as not the principal, as the turn's own check does. Neither scope lets the turn reach anyone. A caller can add privacy but never remove it, and a check that cannot run keeps the row private. On anyone else's turn a contact is a stranger, so a row that names one keeps its visibility: hiding it would tell whoever wrote it that the address belongs to a contact. The poller handles each message with no session bound, so one message's private turn never marks the next message's rows.

Every read route resolves the caller as `/alerts` and `/decisions` do (`people.caller_is_principal`: the principal's signed-in email, or no `x-caller-email` — the CLI, direct curl, local login — once a principal is on the roster; before anyone is principal, nobody). For anyone else private rows are filtered in SQL (`include_private=False` on `query`, `count` and `usage_summary`), so `total` and pagination stay honest: `GET /audit/logs` leaves them out, `GET /audit/logs/{id}` answers 404 exactly as for a missing id, `GET /audit/sessions/{id}` shows only the other rows (404 when none are left), and `GET /audit/usage` leaves out their tokens and cost. Internal readers see every row unless they ask otherwise; the department check-in, whose report goes to the department, reads its recent activity without them, and its "nothing new since the review" skip rule ignores them too. Ids are one autoincrement sequence, so anyone else can still see a gap where a private row was written; that is accepted.

### Views
- `GET /audit` — filterable list with a "Group by session" toggle and session pills.
- `GET /audit/session/{id}` — full ordered timeline plus a server-derived node/edge graph rendered as a three-pane React Flow chart.

### Invariant
Audit writes never break a chat turn: all writes swallow exceptions and log a warning, and instrumentation observes only — it never touches request building or the cached prompt blocks. Audit is append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE paths exist in product code.
